symptom: A JavaScript action with a parameter throws `<Param> is not defined` the first time a user clicks it. `mx check` reports 0 errors, `mxcli check` says nothing, the build is clean, and the generated file cannot be patched — it is rewritten on every build
cause: mxbuild **lowers the first letter** of a parameter when it generates the wrapper: `Skin: String` reaches the body as `skin`. A body written with the modelled spelling is a ReferenceError, and nothing between MDL and the click can see it — Mendix treats the body as opaque user code
file: `cmd/mxcli/theme/switcher.go` (both parameterised actions); the same rule applies to any `create javascript action` with parameters
insight: **Model the parameter capitalised, read it lowercased.** Verified against a real 11.13 build (`export async function SetAppSkin(skin)`) and in a browser by importing the generated module and calling it — `ReferenceError: Skin is not defined` before, the correct return after. The guard walks *every* parameter of *every* generated action, so a new one cannot reintroduce it. Note the trap in writing that guard: a regex anchored on `javascript action` also matches `call javascript action` in the nanoflows, which made the first version run past a real declaration and pass against the very defect it was written for — anchor on `create or modify javascript action` and assert the match count. ako/mxcli-ledger #135
